**TL;DR:** The Blossom-CI `Authorization` job failed because commit `4e9e433` is unsigned, so the `blossom-ci` AUTH step declined the auto-trigger and exited 255 — a policy gate, not a build/code defect; either sign the commit (or have a maintainer comment `/build`), and make the decline path exit non-fatally.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** The `Authorization` job of the Blossom-CI workflow exited 255 at the `blossom-ci` AUTH step for PR #2247; no build, test, or compile step ever ran.

**Root cause:** The workflow was triggered by `pull_request_target` (event auto-trigger path), and the AUTH operation refused to authorize it. The log is unambiguous about the sequence:

- `Workflow file validated against template: blossom-ci-v3.yaml` — the workflow itself is fine.
- `Commit signature not verified (reason=unsigned); declining auto-trigger`
- `PR State: open`
- `Auto-trigger declined: use manual comment trigger`
- `##[error]Process completed with exit code 255.`

So the head commit `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` on `fix_read_me` carries no GPG/SSH signature. Blossom's auto-trigger policy only accepts verified-signature commits for the `pull_request_target` path (it cannot safely run untrusted PR code with secrets otherwise) and falls back to requiring an explicit `/build` comment from an authorized maintainer.

The secondary, more actionable problem is that this *expected* decline is reported as a hard failure. `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` (NirWolfer, 2026-09-07, "CI: Update Blossom CI to support automatic trigger (#2219)") added `pull_request_target: [opened, synchronize, reopened]` to the `on:` list and widened the job condition to `github.event.comment.body == '/build' || (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target')`. Because the AUTH tool exits 255 rather than 0/neutral when it declines, every PR whose commits are unsigned now gets a red ❌ Blossom-CI check on open and on every push, instead of the job simply not proceeding. The log timestamps show the whole job took ~3 seconds with no gaps — there is no hang, timeout, or infrastructure component to this at all.

Note the log also lists several `Untrusted reference action organization` / `Action mismatch` lines (`gradle`, `ravitestgit`, `Ranjeet-Nvidia`). These are template-validation diagnostics emitted before the successful `Workflow file validated against template` line and are not the cause of the exit 255.

**Implicated commit:** `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` — NirWolfer, 2026-09-07, "CI: Update Blossom CI to support automatic trigger (#2219)" (introduced the failing auto-trigger path). The immediate trigger is the unsigned PR commit `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` on `fix_read_me`.

**File:** `.github/workflows/blossom-ci.yml:15-16` (the `pull_request_target` trigger) and `.github/workflows/blossom-ci.yml:33-40` (the `Authorization` job condition and AUTH step)

**Suggested fix:** Two parts — unblock this PR, then stop the false red.

1. To unblock PR #2247 right now, pick either:
   - Have a maintainer comment `/build` on the PR — this is exactly the path the log recommends (`Auto-trigger declined: use manual comment trigger`), and it works regardless of signature.
   - Or have the contributor sign and force-push: enable commit signing (`git config commit.gpgsign true`, or SSH signing via `gpg.format = ssh`), then `git commit --amend -S --no-edit && git push --force-with-lease`. The check should then auto-trigger.

2. To stop unsigned PRs from producing a failed check, make the decline path non-fatal. Least invasive is to let the AUTH step's decline not fail the run when it came from the event trigger:

```yaml
      - name: Check if comment is issued by authorized person
        run: blossom-ci
        continue-on-error: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' }}
        env:
          OPERATION: 'AUTH'
          REPO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPO_KEY_DATA: ${{ secrets.BLOSSOM_KEY }}
```

Downstream jobs already gate on `needs: [Authorization]` and on `fromJson(needs.Authorization.outputs.args)`, so an empty `args` will keep them from running. Better still, ask the Blossom maintainers to have the AUTH operation exit `0` (or emit a neutral conclusion) on the "declining auto-trigger" branch rather than 255, since a policy decline is a normal outcome and not an error. If auto-trigger is not actually wanted for external/unsigned contributions, the alternative is to revert to comment-only triggering by dropping the `pull_request_target` entry at line 15-16 and the `github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'` clause at line 33.

**Related:** PR #2247 (this PR, https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2247); PR #2219 introduced the auto-trigger. Prior history shows this exact area has been churned before — `531e8038` "CI: fix for blossom-ci auto trigger without comment (#771)" was reverted by `8d78f896` (#775), and `d899d0fe` (#748) deliberately avoided `/build`-comment triggering; worth reviewing those before re-tuning the trigger.

</details>

  ```yaml
  - name: Check if comment is issued by authorized person
    id: auth
    run: blossom-ci || { code=$?; [ "$code" -eq 255 ] && echo "auto-trigger declined for external contributor" && exit 0; exit "$code"; }
  ```

  Keeping the security gate intact matters — do **not** widen it to auto-run external code. Downstream jobs already chain via `needs:`, so they stay skipped when `args` is unset.
- Optionally restrict the `pull_request_target` trigger to same-repo branches, letting forks rely solely on the `/build` comment path and avoiding the misleading check entirely.

**Related:** PR #2247 (the affected PR); PR #2219 / commit `[REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String]` (introduced auto-trigger); prior history on this exact behaviour — #771 and its revert #775, plus #748 "CI: avoid /build comment to trigger blossom-ci" — indicating auto-trigger semantics have regressed before.

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-21

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `9a619bd8`

**TL;DR:** The `Test Python` stage on the aarch64/ubuntu22 variant failed because `test_tcpstore_metadata_exchange` could not reach its own PyTorch `TCPStore` master on the CI-assigned port 10507 within the hard-coded 5 s timeout; this is a flaky fixed-port handoff in the CI port allocator, not a defect in the PR (a README-only change), and the fix is to let the test fall back to an OS-assigned port / retry instead of pinning `NIXL_TCPSTORE_PORT`.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** Build #3124, `Parallel` → `Test Python` (stage 574, aarch64 ubuntu22 pod `nixl-ci-non-gpu-base-ubuntu22-3124-fl01w-7smzd`) failed with `1 failed, 24 passed, 3 skipped`: `test/python/test_tcpstore_metadata.py::test_tcpstore_metadata_exchange - torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The client socket has timed out after 5000ms while trying to connect to (127.0.0.1, 10507)`.

**Root cause:** The test constructs `dist.TCPStore(host_name="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["NIXL_TCPSTORE_PORT"]), is_master=True, timeout=5s)` (`test/python/test_tcpstore_metadata.py:21-28`). The port comes from `get_next_tcp_port()` in `.ci/scripts/common.sh:38-61`, which is unreliable:
- It persists a counter in `/tmp/nixl_tcp_port_<id>`; in this pod that file already contained `10504` before the Python stage even started, and the etcd data-dir in the workspace was a stale member advertising `http://127.0.0.1:10502` — i.e. `/tmp` and the workspace carried over from an earlier run, so the port pool is not fresh per build.
- Liveness is checked with `ss -tuln | grep -q :$next_port`, which only sees *listening* sockets. A port held by an established/TIME_WAIT socket (e.g. left by the `Test CPP` stage that ran in the same container immediately before, finishing at 14:03:x) is reported free.
- The check is pure TOCTOU: the port is "reserved" only in a text file, and ~7 s of etcd startup and pip work elapse (14:04:31 → 14:04:34) before pytest actually binds it.

So the store's master socket was not reachable on 10507 and torch retried until its 5 s deadline (the accompanying `[c10d] The hostname of the client socket cannot be retrieved. err=-3` shows the resolver was also unhappy in that container). The same test passed in the five other parallel variants of this very build, and the commit under test (`9a619bd`, branch `fix_read_me`, PR #2247) touches documentation only — it cannot produce this failure.

**Implicated commit:** aed5ef2e — "test: add Python TCPStore metadata integration (#2148)", aschwartz12 (added both the test and the `NIXL_TCPSTORE_PORT` export); the underlying port allocator is f125c7bc / 43ffb37f by Alexey Rivkin / Roie Danino.

**File:** `test/python/test_tcpstore_metadata.py:21-28` (with `.gitlab/test_python.sh:70-71` and `.ci/scripts/common.sh:38-61`)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Make the test resilient instead of depending on a pre-assigned port: wrap the `TCPStore` construction in a retry that falls back to `port=0` (kernel-assigned, which the test already supports via `tcp_store.port`) on `DistNetworkError`, and raise the `timeout` from 5 s to ~30 s so a loaded aarch64 executor doesn't trip it.
2. Harden `get_next_tcp_port()` in `.ci/scripts/common.sh`: probe by actually binding (e.g. `python3 -c "import socket;s=socket.socket();s.bind(('127.0.0.1',$p))"`) rather than grepping `ss -tuln`, anchor the grep (`grep -qE "[:.]$next_port\$"`), and clear `/tmp/nixl_tcp_port_*` plus the stale `default.etcd` data-dir at the start of each build so state does not leak between runs on a reused agent.
3. Short term: re-run build #3124 — this is an infrastructure flake unrelated to PR #2247.

**Related:** PR #2148 (introduced the test and port wiring); PR #1685 / #568 (CI TCP port pool). No existing issue tracks this flake.

</details>
